sections.executive_summary:
Florida assisted living facilities (ALFs) are licensed by the Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA) under Chapter 429, Part I, Florida Statutes, Chapter 408, Part II, F.S., and rule chapter 59A-36, F.A.C. [S12][S11]. A standard license covers housing, meals and personal services. Three optional specialty licenses let residents age in place: Extended Congregate Care (ECC), Limited Nursing Services (LNS) and Limited Mental Health (LMH) [S1].

**The market is large and mostly private pay.** NCAL counts 2,968 assisted living communities with 117,384 beds or units in Florida, and reports that 24% of residents rely on Medicaid for long-term care [S43]. Persons 65 and over are 22.8% of Florida's 23.46 million residents (V2025) [S57]. CareScout's 2025 survey puts the Florida assisted living median at $66,000 a year, about $5,500 a month, up 3% from 2024 [S41].

**Medicaid does not pay a published state rate.** Florida Medicaid covers assisted living only through the Statewide Medicaid Managed Care (SMMC) Long-Term Care program. LTC plans and facilities "negotiate mutually acceptable rates" [S30], so no state rate table exists. LTC enrollment is not an entitlement. The Department of Elder Affairs releases people from a priority-ranked wait list as slots open [S33][S34]. Low-income residents often pay room and board through SSI plus Optional State Supplementation (OSS). The OSS base provider rate is $991.40 a month, room and board only [S37].

**The profitable path is private pay at 10–16 beds or 30+ beds with a specialty license.** The model in Section 8 uses real staffing rules, BLS May 2025 Florida wages and the CareScout median. A 6-bed private-pay home is roughly break-even with a paid administrator and works mainly when the owner runs it. A 14-bed home stays under the 17-resident awake-overnight threshold [S5] and is the strongest small-facility model. A 36-bed facility with an LNS license earns the highest margin. Medicaid-heavy payer mixes lose money at the public floor rates. Medicaid only works where an LTC plan contract rate covers care costs.

### Key Numbers (Verified)
See the Key Numbers table. Every figure traces to a source listed in this report.

### What This Report Does Not Claim
See the list at the end of this summary. Where the prior report made numerical claims we could not verify (Medicaid "tier" rates, market shares, a $1,000–$1,565 license fee), we removed them rather than replace them with estimates.
sections.service_model:
### Who is served
ALF residents must be at least 18 and able to perform activities of daily living with supervision or assistance. They must be able to transfer (with help if needed), not be bedridden (except under hospice), have no stage 3 or 4 pressure sores, and not need 24-hour licensed mental health treatment [S19]. Each resident needs a medical exam within 60 days before or 30 days after admission, recorded on AHCA Form 1823 or the practitioner's form [S66][S19]. NCAL's Florida profile shows 70% of residents are women, 45% are 85 or older, 47% have Alzheimer's or other dementia, and 63% need help bathing [S43].

### License types
- **Standard** — personal services, supervision and medication assistance. Licensed nurses may be employed or contracted to administer medications [S1].
- **Limited Nursing Services (LNS)** — nursing for residents who do not need 24-hour nursing supervision, and for residents who need 24-hour care and are enrolled in hospice. The facility employs or contracts a nurse, needs practitioner orders and does monthly nursing assessments [S8]. You may apply at initial licensure [S2].
- **Extended Congregate Care (ECC)** — any nursing service within license scope under a service plan, so residents who would otherwise be disqualified can stay. A facility licensed under 2 years gets only a provisional ECC license of no more than 6 months [S1][S7].
- **Limited Mental Health (LMH)** — required before admitting any mental health resident. Needs a standard license and no uncorrected violations, staff mental health training, and each resident's community living support plan and cooperative agreement [S10][S9]. No extra AHCA fee [S2].

### Regulatory framework
AHCA's Assisted Living Unit licenses and surveys facilities [S12]. County health departments inspect food hygiene and sanitation. The local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects fire safety. County emergency management approves emergency plans [S21][S17]. The rules were renumbered from chapter 58A-5 to 59A-36 on July 1, 2019. Examples: staffing is now 59A-36.010 (formerly 58A-5.019), emergency management 59A-36.019, resident contracts 59A-36.018, medication 59A-36.008, LMH 59A-36.020, ECC 59A-36.021 and LNS 59A-36.022 [S11][S5].

### Zoning by size
A home of six or fewer residents counts as a single-family residential use and is allowed in single-family or multifamily zoning without local approval. It must not be within 1,000 feet of a similar home or 1,200 feet of a community residential home [S25]. Homes of 7–14 residents are community residential homes and go through the local notice and site-selection process [S25]. Larger facilities need zoning that allows ALF use.
sections.licensing_pathway:
### Step-by-step
1. **Form the entity and choose size and license scope.** LLC filing is $100 plus $25 for the registered agent designation [S53].
2. **Secure a compliant site.** Confirm zoning and ch. 419 spacing [S25] and building and fire code compliance [S20]. Size the generator to keep temperature at or below 81°F for 96 hours, with 48 hours of fuel onsite (16 or fewer beds) or 72 hours (17+ beds) [S18].
3. **Qualify the administrator.** Age 21+, high school diploma or GED, Level 2 screening. Complete 26 hours of core training and pass the competency test with 75% within 90 days of becoming administrator. Test fee is up to $200 per attempt [S5][S6][S13].
4. **Screen owners and staff.** Level 2 fingerprinting through AHCA's Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse, with rescreening every 5 years [S26][S27][S28][S29].
5. **Bind liability insurance** (required at all times, no dollar minimum in rule) [S15][S14]. **Add workers' compensation** once you have four or more employees [S48].
6. **Write the CEMP** on AHCA Form 3180-5006 and get county emergency management approval [S17]. Submit the Emergency Environmental Control Plan before licensure [S18].
7. **Pass local inspections:** fire safety, the DOH Residential Group Care (sanitation) inspection, and a food hygiene inspection for 11+ beds [S21][S2].
8. **File AHCA Form 3110-1008** through the Online Licensing System [S58] with the required attachments. These include the liability certificate, EECP approval and Consumer Friendly Summary, inspection reports, zoning documentation, Proof of Financial Ability to Operate, the administrator's diploma, proof of occupancy, the visitation policy and the Form 3110-1024 addendum [S2]. Missing items must reach AHCA within 21 days of an omission notice or the application is withdrawn [S2].
9. **AHCA survey, then license.** You may not operate without a license [S1].

### Fees (biennial license)
Section 429.07(4), F.S. sets the base fee at $300 per license plus $50 per resident (OSS beds exempt), capped at $10,000. ECC adds $400 + $10 per resident and LNS adds $250 + $10 per resident [S1]. Section 408.805(2) lets AHCA raise fees each year by CPI [S4], so AHCA actually charges higher amounts. The current application lists $387.73 + $64.96 per private-pay bed (cap $14,253.64), ECC $546.07 + $10.15/bed, LNS $322.77 + $10.15/bed, LMH $0, plus a $2.00/bed biennial assessment capped at $300 [S2][S3]. Examples: 6 beds = $789.49; 14 beds = $1,325.17; 36 beds with LNS = $3,486.46.

### Timeline
AHCA does not publish a processing standard for initial ALF licenses. The binding deadlines are the 21-day omission response window [S2] and the 90-day administrator core training deadline [S5]. Plan the full calendar around your local zoning, fire and county emergency management reviews, which vary by county.
sections.reimbursement:
### How money flows
1. **Private pay (dominant).** Residents and families pay a monthly rate under the resident contract. The contract must list services, rates, extra charges and a 30-day notice before increases [S68][S63]. CareScout: Florida median $66,000/year in 2025, about $5,500/month [S41]; $63,885 in 2024 [S42]. The CareScout median is for a private one-bedroom unit in an assisted living community; shared-room rates in small residential homes are typically lower, so price from local comparables.
2. **SMMC Long-Term Care plans (Medicaid).** Assisted living is a covered LTC service [S33]. AHCA contracts LTC plans. The plans contract with ALFs and must negotiate "mutually acceptable rates, methods, and terms of payment" [S30]. AHCA pays plans a capitation rate, not per-facility rates [S31]. **No public state rate table exists for ALF services.** Your rate is whatever you negotiate with each plan. Medicaid cannot pay for room and board in assisted living [S56]. Enrollees must meet nursing facility level of care, be screened by an ADRC, and be released from the priority-ranked wait list [S33][S34]. Plans were re-procured under ITN 010-22/23 [S62]. Current plans by region are on AHCA's SMMC page [S61].
3. **Optional State Supplementation (OSS).** A DCF cash supplement for low-income ALF residents on SSI. The resident pays the facility the OSS base provider rate, $991.40/month for room and board (rule effective 6/24/2025), and keeps a $160 personal needs allowance [S37]. OSS rates rise with the federal SSI COLA [S36][S37]. The 2026 SSI federal rate is $994/month [S40]. Third parties may add voluntary supplementation, paid to the facility, up to four times the OSS provider rate [S36]. OSS beds are exempt from the AHCA per-bed license fee, based on the prior period's average OSS census [S2][S23].
4. **Medicaid Assistive Care Services (ACS).** T1020 pays $15.58/day (2026, effective 1/1/2026) for qualifying non-waiver Medicaid residents [S38][S39].

### What it means for a new operator
A low-income resident on OSS and ACS brings in about $1,465 a month ($991.40 + $15.58 × 30.42 days). That is roughly a quarter of the private-pay median. GAO reports that officials from one state and representatives from one organization said Medicaid assisted living rates are often about one-third of private-pay rates, which discourages participation [S56]. The model treats LTC plan contract rates as unknown until you negotiate them. It uses the public ACS rate as a floor, so Medicaid-mix configurations are conservative.
sections.demand:
### Demographics
Florida has 23,462,518 residents (V2025), and 22.8% are 65 or older [S57]. Assisted living residents in Florida are mostly women (70%) and very old (45% are 85+). Nearly half have dementia [S43].

### Medicaid LTC demand
The SMMC LTC wait list is managed by DOEA through ADRCs. Release depends on priority score and frailty rank, not time on the list [S34]. A public records response to the Florida Assisted Living Association showed 43,335 people on the LTC wait list on October 2, 2023. The largest group, 12,511, was 85 or older [S55]. GAO reports Florida expected to serve more than 20,000 Medicaid assisted living beneficiaries a year, one of four states above that level [S56].

### Referral sources
- Hospital and rehabilitation discharge planners
- Home health and hospice agencies
- SMMC LTC plan case managers (for Medicaid enrollees)
- ADRCs and Medicaid choice counseling (1-877-711-3662) [S35]
- Fee-based senior placement agencies, physicians and elder law attorneys

### Occupancy
NIC MAP reports assisted living occupancy of 88.4% in its 31 primary markets in 2Q 2026 [S44]. The model uses 90% at stabilization as the default — an operator target 1.6 points above the NIC figure — and shows 85% and 95% cases.
sections.operations:
### Minimum staffing (Rule 59A-36.010)
The weekly staff-hour minimums by combined residents, day care participants and respite residents are: 0–5 = 168; 6–15 = 212; 16–25 = 253; 26–35 = 294; 36–45 = 335; 46–55 = 375; 56–65 = 416; 66–75 = 457; 76–85 = 498; 86–95 = 539; plus 42 hours for every 20 over 95 [S5].
- A staff member with access to records must be in the facility whenever residents are present.
- **At 17 or more residents, at least one staff member must be awake at all hours.** Below 17 the rule does not require awake overnight staff, though someone must still be present [S5].
- A staff member with current First Aid and CPR must be in the facility at all times [S5].
- The administrator or manager's hours count if they are on the schedule and active in daily care. Staff working only in maintenance, clerical or food preparation do not count [S5].
- AHCA can order staffing above the minimum when resident needs are not met [S5].
- LMH, ECC and LNS facilities must also meet the staffing rules in 59A-36.020, .021 and .022 [S5]. ECC requires adequate awake staff at all hours and a nurse on staff or under contract [S7]. LNS requires a nurse available as needed [S8].
- One administrator may oversee up to three ALFs, with managers appointed in writing [S5].

### Training (Rule 59A-36.011; s. 429.52)
- **Administrator:** 26-hour core training plus a competency test (75% to pass) within 90 days; 12 hours CE every 2 years [S6][S13].
- **Staff:** 2-hour preservice orientation; 1 hour infection control before personal care; within 30 days, 1 hour adverse incidents and emergency procedures, 1 hour resident rights and abuse, 3 hours behavior and ADLs, elopement training and HIV/AIDS [S6].
- **Medication assistance by unlicensed staff:** 6 hours initial with an RN or pharmacist certificate, then 2 hours a year [S6][S13].
- **ECC:** 4 hours for the administrator and ECC supervisor, plus 4 hours CE every 2 years; 2 hours for direct care staff [S6].
- **LMH:** 6 hours within 6 months, then 3 hours every 2 years [S6][S10].

### Required systems and plans
- Annual CEMP approved by county emergency management [S17]
- 96-hour emergency power plan [S18]
- An AED at 17+ beds [S24]
- Separate resident trust accounting [S14]
- A written 24-hour staffing schedule [S5]
- Records per 59A-36.015 [S65]

Florida has no EVV mandate for ALFs. An eMAR is an operator choice.
sections.market_conditions:
### Supply
NCAL reports 2,968 assisted living communities and 117,384 beds or units in Florida [S43]. This report does not claim regional saturation or competitor shares.

### Pricing
The Florida private-pay median was $66,000/year in 2025, about $5,500/month, up 3% from 2024. The national median was $74,400/year [S41]. The 2024 Florida median was $63,885 [S42]. The CareScout figure measures a private one-bedroom unit in an assisted living community; shared-room rates in 6–14 bed residential homes are typically lower and no public Florida small-home price source exists, so price from local comparables. Medicaid pays much less (Section 4).

### Wages (BLS OEWS May 2025, Florida medians) [S45]
- Home health and personal care aides: $16.25/hr
- Nursing assistants: $18.03
- LPNs: $29.70
- RNs: $40.48
- Institutional cooks: $17.43
- Housekeepers: $16.28
- Maintenance: $22.15
- Medical and health services managers: 10th percentile $33.61, 25th percentile $44.49

Florida's minimum wage rose to $15.00/hour on September 30, 2026, and will be CPI-indexed from January 1, 2028 [S46][S47]. The aide median is only $1.25 above the new floor, so expect wage pressure.

### Employer costs
- Employer FICA: 7.65% [S51]
- Florida reemployment tax: 2.7% on the first $7,000 for new employers [S49][S50]
- FUTA [S52]
- Workers' comp: mandatory at four or more employees [S48]

### Housing costs
HUD's FY2027 Small Area Fair Market Rent for a 4-bedroom home in an Orlando-area ZIP is $3,020 [S54]. Rents in southeast Florida are higher — verify locally.
sections.financial_narrative:
### How the P&L is built
Revenue per resident × occupied residents, minus staffing (with payroll burden) and operating costs. Default occupancy is 90% [S44]. Ramp-up is set per configuration: the 6-bed homes start at 2 residents and add 1 per month, the 14-bed home starts at 2 and adds 2 per month, and the 36-bed facilities start at 4 and add 3 per month (operator planning assumptions — verify against your referral pipeline).

**Revenue.** Private pay uses the CareScout 2025 Florida median of $5,500/month [S41]. That median is for a private one-bedroom unit in an assisted living community; shared-room rates in small residential homes are typically lower, so the 6- and 14-bed results may be optimistic — price from local comparables. Medicaid-mix configurations model low-income residents at the OSS base provider rate of $991.40 [S37] plus the public ACS rate of $15.58/day [S38]. That is a floor. Replace it with your negotiated SMMC LTC plan rate, which is not public [S30].

**Staffing.** Every configuration meets the Rule 59A-36.010 weekly-hours table and 24-hour presence rules [S5], at BLS May 2025 Florida wages [S45], all above the $15.00 minimum [S46]. Configurations under 17 residents have no awake-overnight mandate. Those at 17+ staff awake overnight. Administrator pay uses Florida BLS manager percentiles: 10th percentile for small homes, 25th for larger ones.

**Burden.** 8.3% payroll taxes, 4% workers' comp and 5% benefits. The comp and benefits rates are estimates.

**Operating costs.**
- Lease is a fixed cost from day one, sized at $578.83 per licensed bed from HUD FMR [S54] (6 beds $3,473; 14 beds $8,104; 36 beds $20,838 — larger buildings are an operator estimate)
- Utilities split into a fixed base load per licensed bed plus a per-resident portion (operator estimate)
- AHCA biennial license and assessment fees, including LNS/ECC fees where held, are amortized monthly per licensed bed [S2]
- Liability insurance is required by law, with the premium estimated [S14]
- Generator fuel and service are required by Rule 59A-36.025 [S18]
- Food, utilities, supplies, software, accounting, marketing, training and transportation are operator estimates, labeled as such

### Results at 90% occupancy (monthly, approximate)
| Configuration | Revenue | Staffing | Opex | Net |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-bed private pay | $29,700 | $21,000 | $9,200 | about –$500 |
| 6-bed mixed (2 low-income) | $22,400 | $21,000 | $9,200 | about –$7,800 |
| 14-bed private pay | $69,300 | $31,600 | $19,200 | about +$18,500 |
| 36-bed LNS private pay | $178,200 | $69,900 | $46,800 | about +$61,500 |
| 36-bed ECC, 25% low-income | $145,500 | $69,900 | $46,800 | about +$28,800 |

### Key drivers
- **Private-pay rate.** Each $250/month on 12.6 residents moves a 14-bed home by about $3,150/month.
- **Size relative to the 17-resident line.** Crossing it adds awake-overnight labor, an AED and more fuel storage.
- **Owner as administrator.** That removes about $6,830/month on a 6-bed home including payroll burden ($5,826 salary + 17.3% burden) and makes it profitable.
- **Medicaid share.** Every low-income bed at floor rates gives up about $4,000/month versus private pay.

The generator calculates break-even from these inputs.
sections.risks:
- **Medicaid rate risk.** No published LTC rate exists. Plans negotiate individually [S30], and low Medicaid rates discourage facility participation [S56]. Do not count on Medicaid revenue until you have a signed plan contract and rate.
- **Wage floor.** The $15.00 minimum wage (Sept 30, 2026) and CPI indexing from 2028 [S46] squeeze margins at aide medians of $16.25 [S45].
- **Hurricane and emergency compliance.** The 96-hour, 81°F generator rule and annual CEMP approval carry real capital and operating costs. Evacuations must be reported within 6 hours [S18][S17].
- **Survey and enforcement.** AHCA can order staffing above the minimum [S5]. A class I or II violation, or repeated class III violations, can block ECC eligibility for 2 years [S1].
- **Specialty license timing.** ECC is provisional for 6 months for facilities licensed under 2 years [S1]. LMH requires no uncorrected violations [S10].
- **Zoning and spacing.** The 1,000/1,200-foot spacing rule for six-or-fewer homes [S25] can rule out properties in dense ALF markets.
- **Resident funds.** Acting as payee or POA requires surety bonds and quarterly statements [S16][S14].
- **Unlicensed activity.** Operating without a license is prohibited. AHCA publishes substantiated unlicensed locations [S1][S12].
- **Occupancy ramp.** Fixed costs (administrator, lease, insurance) run from day one. Size your working capital for a 6–12 month fill.
sections.recommendations:
1. **Lead with private pay at 10–16 beds.** The 14-bed configuration stays under the 17-resident awake-overnight line [S5]. It is profitable at the CareScout median [S41] with full rule-compliant staffing. Get ch. 419 site approval and a DOH food hygiene inspection for 11+ beds [S25][S2].
2. **For a 6-bed home, run it as owner-administrator.** Hire for the remaining 172 caregiver hours a week. Price at or above the local median, and charge care-level add-ons in the contract [S63].
3. **Add LNS at licensing if you plan to keep residents longer.** It costs $322.77 + $10.15/bed per biennium [S2]. It reduces move-outs from rising care needs and supports premium pricing. A new facility can apply for ECC before it has 2 years of history: it receives a provisional ECC license of up to 6 months, followed by an unannounced inspection [S1]. Many operators still wait until operations are stable.
4. **Treat Medicaid as a selective add-on.** Limit low-income beds to a share your private-pay margin can carry. Negotiate rates in writing with each LTC plan in your region [S30][S61]. Use OSS-designated beds to reduce license fees [S2].
5. **Budget for Florida-specific capital.** That means the generator and fuel storage [S18], fire safety [S21], and furnishings to Rule 59A-36.014 [S20].
6. **Build compliance in from day one.** Have the administrator's core training and test done before opening [S6]. Use the Clearinghouse for all screening [S28]. Keep the CEMP calendar [S17], track staff training [S6], and file annual inspections within 30 days [S22].
7. **Ramp with referrals.** Work hospital discharge planners, home health and hospice agencies, ADRCs, and LTC plan case managers (if contracted).

checklist.task: Decide license scope and size before anything else
checklist.instructions: Choose a standard license, and whether you will later add LNS, ECC or LMH. Choose your size: 1–6 residents (single-family use), 7–14 (community residential home, needs local site approval), or 15+ (commercial zoning). Crossing 16→17 residents adds the awake-overnight rule, an AED, 72 hours of onsite generator fuel and a different Proof of Financial Ability form.

checklist.task: Form a Florida legal entity
checklist.instructions: File Articles of Organization for an LLC on Sunbiz (Division of Corporations). Statutory fee is $100 plus $25 for the registered agent designation. The licensee named on the AHCA application must match this entity exactly.

checklist.task: Obtain an EIN from the IRS
checklist.instructions: Free at irs.gov and issued online the same day. Needed for payroll, banking, the AHCA application and insurance.

checklist.task: Register with the Florida Department of Revenue for reemployment tax
checklist.instructions: Register as an employer before the first payroll. New employers pay 2.7% on the first $7,000 of each employee's wages.

checklist.task: Open separate operating and resident trust bank accounts
checklist.instructions: Facility funds and resident funds may not be co-mingled. One trust account is allowed if you keep a separate written accounting for each resident.

checklist.task: Obtain a local business tax receipt
checklist.instructions: Apply with the county and/or city tax collector once you have the address. Fees vary by jurisdiction — verify locally.

checklist.task: Prepare an ownership and controlling-interest roster
checklist.instructions: List every owner, officer, administrator and management company. You need it for the Health Care Licensing Application Addendum (AHCA Form 3110-1024) and for Level 2 screening of controlling interests.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Confirm zoning in writing before signing a lease
checklist.instructions: Homes of six or fewer residents are a single-family residential use. They are allowed without local approval if no similar home is within 1,000 ft and no community residential home is within 1,200 ft. Bring the licensing-entity list of nearby homes to the local government. Homes of 7–14 residents follow the s. 419.001 notice and site-selection process. Local zoning documentation is a required AHCA attachment.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Verify the building meets the Florida Building Code and fire standards for ALF use
checklist.instructions: New construction and conversions must meet Florida Building Code Ch. 4 §464, the Uniform Fire Safety Standards for ALFs (ch. 69A-40, F.A.C.) and the NFPA codes in s. 429.41, F.S. Hire an architect or code consultant for any conversion and ask the local fire authority about sprinklers early.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Plan resident rooms and furnishings to rule
checklist.instructions: If you supply furnishings, each resident needs a bed with a mattress at least 36"×72", closet or wardrobe space, a dresser, a nightstand or table, a lamp, a wastebasket and a chair on request. Keep master keys to bedrooms. Provide linens and laundry service.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Size the emergency power system for 96 hours at ≤81°F
checklist.instructions: You need an alternate power source (generator) that keeps the cooled area at or below 81°F for 96 hours. Allow at least 20 net sq ft per resident, using 80% of licensed capacity. Store 48 hours of fuel onsite (16 or fewer beds) or 72 hours (17+ beds). Piped natural gas counts. You also need a carbon monoxide alarm.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Confirm water and sewer service or schedule a septic/well evaluation
checklist.instructions: If on septic or a private well, a DOH septic or water supply evaluation report is a required attachment for initial licensure.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Document proof of property occupancy
checklist.instructions: Have a signed lease, deed/mortgage or transfer agreement in the licensee's name. It is a required attachment.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Buy an AED if licensed for 17+ beds
checklist.instructions: Facilities with 17 or more beds must have a working automated external defibrillator on the premises at all times.

checklist.task: Designate a qualified administrator
checklist.instructions: Administrator must be at least 21, have a high school diploma or GED, and clear Level 2 screening. A copy of the diploma or GED is a required attachment. One administrator may oversee up to three ALFs.

checklist.task: Complete the 26-hour core training and pass the competency test (75%)
checklist.instructions: Take the AHCA-approved core training (minimum 26 hours) and pass the competency test with at least 75%. This must be done within 90 days of becoming the administrator. Test fee is up to $200 per attempt. Licensed nursing home administrators are exempt from core training under the statute. Doing it before you open avoids risk.

checklist.task: Run Level 2 background screening through the Clearinghouse
checklist.instructions: Screen the administrator, controlling interests and all staff (including contracted staff who serve residents) with Level 2 fingerprinting through the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse. Rescreen every 5 years. Clearinghouse help line: 850-412-4503.

checklist.task: Appoint managers if one administrator runs multiple homes
checklist.instructions: An administrator over more than one facility must appoint a manager in writing for each. Up to three homes of 16 or fewer beds within 15 miles need only two managers. Managers meet the same training and screening rules.

checklist.task: Plan staff training to the rule
checklist.instructions: Covers: 2-hour preservice orientation before working with residents; 1 hour of infection control before giving personal care; within 30 days, 1 hour of adverse incidents and emergency procedures, 1 hour of resident rights and abuse reporting, 3 hours of resident behavior and ADLs, elopement training and HIV/AIDS. A 6-hour medication assistance course with an RN or pharmacist certificate is required before unlicensed staff assist with medications, then 2 hours each year.

checklist.task: Keep a CPR/First Aid–certified staff member on site at all times
checklist.instructions: Schedule so at least one person with a current First Aid and CPR card (in-person skills demonstration) is in the facility around the clock.

checklist.task: Train food service lead
checklist.instructions: If the food service designee has not completed core training, they must complete its food and nutrition module, unless they are a certified food or dietary manager, dietitian or similar.

checklist.phase: PHASE 4 — INSURANCE, FINANCIAL ABILITY & RESIDENT FUNDS
checklist.task: Bind general/professional liability insurance
checklist.instructions: Coverage must be in force at all times. The certificate must show the facility's name, street address, that it is an ALF, licensed capacity and coverage dates. File it with AHCA at each renewal or policy change. No dollar minimum is set in rule; carriers commonly quote $1M/$3M — verify.

checklist.phase: PHASE 4 — INSURANCE, FINANCIAL ABILITY & RESIDENT FUNDS
checklist.task: Buy workers' compensation once you have 4 or more employees
checklist.instructions: Workers' comp is mandatory for private employers with four or more employees, part-time included.

checklist.phase: PHASE 4 — INSURANCE, FINANCIAL ABILITY & RESIDENT FUNDS
checklist.task: Complete Proof of Financial Ability to Operate
checklist.instructions: Use AHCA's form for ALFs with 16 or fewer beds, or Form 3100-0009 for 17+ beds. Show startup costs and operating reserves. Required for initial and change of ownership.

checklist.phase: PHASE 4 — INSURANCE, FINANCIAL ABILITY & RESIDENT FUNDS
checklist.task: Get a surety bond if you will be representative payee or hold power of attorney
checklist.instructions: As representative payee the bond must equal twice the average monthly aggregate resident income you receive. Under a power of attorney it is per resident: twice monthly income plus property held. File a copy with AHCA each year.

checklist.phase: PHASE 4 — INSURANCE, FINANCIAL ABILITY & RESIDENT FUNDS
checklist.task: Set up resident funds accounting
checklist.instructions: Safekeep up to $500 cash and $500 in effects by mutual consent. Give each resident a verified statement at least every 3 months.

checklist.task: Write the resident contract
checklist.instructions: Must list services, the daily, weekly or monthly rate, extra charges, 30-day notice before rate increases, deposit and refund policy, bed hold policy, religious affiliation and transfer notice. Executed at or before admission.

checklist.task: Write admission and continued-residency criteria
checklist.instructions: Residents must be 18+, able to do ADLs with assistance, able to transfer with help, not bedridden (except hospice), no stage 3–4 pressure sores, and not needing 24-hour licensed mental health treatment. Get a medical exam on AHCA Form 1823 (or the practitioner's form) within 60 days before or 30 days after admission.

checklist.task: Write medication policies
checklist.instructions: Cover self-administration, assistance with self-administration by trained unlicensed staff (with written informed consent), administration by licensed nurses only, storage and records.

checklist.task: Write staffing plan and 24-hour schedule
checklist.instructions: Keep a written 24-hour work schedule. Meet the 59A-36.010 weekly-hours table: 168 hrs for 0–5 residents, 212 for 6–15, 253 for 16–25, 294 for 26–35, 335 for 36–45, then +42 per 20 residents over 95. Count only on-the-job care staff. The administrator counts if on the schedule and active in care. Staff working only in food, maintenance or clerical roles do not count.

checklist.task: Write resident rights, grievance and abuse reporting policies
checklist.instructions: Post the Florida Abuse Hotline (1-800-962-2873). Train staff on recognizing and reporting abuse, neglect and exploitation within 30 days of hire.

checklist.task: Write elopement prevention and response policy
checklist.instructions: All staff must be trained within 30 days and show competency.

checklist.task: Write visitation policy
checklist.instructions: A visitation policy and procedure is a required attachment for initial and renewal applications.

checklist.task: Write food service policy and menus
checklist.instructions: Meet 59A-36.012 food service standards. Name the food service designee in writing.

checklist.task: Set up records system
checklist.instructions: Display the license. Keep an admission and discharge log, resident records, staff records (screening, training, licenses) and accounting records.

checklist.task: Prepare the Consumer Friendly Summary
checklist.instructions: AHCA posts a template. It is submitted with the Emergency Environmental Control Plan approval for initial licensure.

checklist.task: Write dementia/ADRD policies if you advertise memory care or have secured areas
checklist.instructions: Facilities that advertise special Alzheimer's/dementia care or keep secured areas must train staff under s. 430.5025, F.S.

checklist.task: Write the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP)
checklist.instructions: Use AHCA Form 3180-5006 (Sept 2023). Cover all hazards, sheltering in place, evacuation, receiving evacuees, residents with ADRD or mobility limits, and county coordination.

checklist.task: Get county emergency management approval of the CEMP
checklist.instructions: The county emergency management agency is the final authority. Submit every year, and within 30 days of any significant change. Contacts are listed at floridadisaster.org/counties.

checklist.task: Submit the Emergency Environmental Control Plan (generator plan) and get approval
checklist.instructions: A new ALF must submit this plan before obtaining a license. The approval letter is a required AHCA attachment.

checklist.task: Pass the fire safety inspection
checklist.instructions: Local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects under s. 429.41, F.S. and ch. 69A-40, F.A.C. The report is required for initial and renewal applications.

checklist.task: Pass the county health department Residential Group Care inspection
checklist.instructions: County health department inspects sanitation (ch. 64E-12), food hygiene and biomedical waste. The report is required.

checklist.task: Get a DOH food hygiene inspection if 11 or more beds
checklist.instructions: Required attachment for all application types for providers with 11+ beds.

checklist.task: Train all staff on the emergency plan within 30 days of hire
checklist.instructions: Report any evacuation to county EM and AHCA within 6 hours of the order.

checklist.task: Download the current ALF application (AHCA Form 3110-1008) and checklist
checklist.instructions: Get them from AHCA's HQA Applications for Licensure page. The old 'Form 3110-1023' cited in prior materials is not the ALF application.

checklist.task: Create AHCA portal access for the Online Licensing System
checklist.instructions: Register, submit the signed User Agreement, and wait about 3 business days for access. Initial applications may be filed online. Renewals must be filed online (effective March 5, 2024).

checklist.task: Calculate and pay licensure fees
checklist.instructions: Standard: $387.73 + $64.96 per private-pay bed (OSS beds exempt), capped at $14,253.64, plus a $2.00/bed biennial assessment (max $300). Example: 6 beds = $789.49; 14 beds = $1,325.17. Fees are nonrefundable. Statute shows the pre-CPI base ($300 + $50/bed, cap $10,000); AHCA charges the CPI-adjusted amounts on the form.

checklist.task: Assemble required attachments
checklist.instructions: Liability certificate, EECP approval and Consumer Friendly Summary, fire report, DOH Residential Group Care report, septic/water report if applicable, DOH food hygiene report (11+ beds), zoning documentation, ch. 419 site documentation (7–14 residents), Proof of Financial Ability, administrator diploma or GED, proof of occupancy, visitation policy, Form 3110-1024 addendum.

checklist.task: Answer omission notices within 21 days
checklist.instructions: The application is withdrawn if missing documents or fees are not received within 21 days of an omission notice.

checklist.task: Prepare for the AHCA initial licensure survey
checklist.instructions: AHCA inspects everything not covered by the fire authority or county health department. Use AHCA's ALF Survey Tags list for a mock survey.

checklist.task: Do not admit residents until the license is issued
checklist.instructions: A license is required to operate an ALF. AHCA publishes lists of substantiated unlicensed ALF locations.

checklist.task: Recruit and price staff at or above Florida minimum wage
checklist.instructions: Minimum wage is $15.00/hour from September 30, 2026 (CPI-indexed from Jan 1, 2028). FL median for home health and personal care aides is $16.25/hour (May 2025).

checklist.task: Set private-pay pricing from local comparables
checklist.instructions: CareScout 2025 Florida median is $66,000/year (about $5,500/month) for a private one-bedroom unit in an assisted living community; shared rooms in small homes typically price lower. Survey 5–10 local ALFs and price care levels above the base.

checklist.task: Build referral relationships
checklist.instructions: Main sources: hospital and rehab discharge planners, home health and hospice agencies, SMMC LTC plan case managers, Aging and Disability Resource Centers, placement agencies (fee-based) and elder law attorneys.

checklist.task: Contract with SMMC LTC plans if you will serve Medicaid residents
checklist.instructions: Florida Medicaid pays for assisted living through SMMC Long-Term Care plans. The facility and each plan negotiate rates (no state rate table). Ask each LTC plan in your region for its credentialing packet and rate offer. Plan contacts for providers are on AHCA's SMMC page.

checklist.task: Learn OSS for low-income residents
checklist.instructions: OSS-eligible residents pay the facility the OSS base provider rate (room & board) and keep a $160 personal needs allowance. Rule 65A-2.036 lists $991.40/month (eff. 6/24/2025, COLA-adjusted yearly). DCF determines eligibility. Any third-party supplementation goes to the facility, is voluntary, and may not exceed four times the OSS provider rate.

checklist.task: Enroll as a Medicaid Assistive Care Services provider if serving non-waiver Medicaid residents
checklist.instructions: ACS (T1020) pays $15.58/day (2026 fee schedule, eff. 1/1/2026) for qualifying non-waiver Medicaid residents.

checklist.task: Set up eMAR / care documentation
checklist.instructions: No EVV mandate applies to Florida ALFs. Good documentation supports survey compliance and plan audits.

checklist.task: Submit fire and sanitation inspection reports to AHCA every year
checklist.instructions: Send copies to AHCA Central Office within 30 days of each annual inspection.

checklist.task: Renew the license every two years, online, at least 60 days early
checklist.instructions: Renewals filed less than 60 days before expiration incur a late fee. Pay the biennial license and assessment fees.

checklist.task: Administrator continuing education — 12 hours every 2 years
checklist.instructions: Keep certificates in the personnel file.

checklist.task: Annual medication-assistance CE (2 hrs) for unlicensed staff
checklist.instructions: Track in personnel records.

checklist.task: Re-submit the CEMP every year
checklist.instructions: Submit to county emergency management. Include proof of submission with your renewal.

checklist.task: Rescreen staff every 5 years (Level 2)
checklist.instructions: Use the Clearinghouse.

checklist.task: Get prior AHCA approval before changing capacity or use of space
checklist.instructions: Capacity changes need AHCA Central Office approval. Converting space to resident use needs Field Office approval.

checklist.task: Keep liability insurance continuous and file proof at each renewal or policy change
checklist.instructions: Coverage must remain in force at all times.

checklist.phase: PHASE 10 — OPTIONAL SPECIALTY LICENSES (LNS, ECC, LMH)
checklist.task: Limited Nursing Services (LNS) license
checklist.instructions: Can be applied for at initial licensure. Employ or contract a nurse available as needed. Services require a practitioner's order. Keep monthly nursing assessments and nursing progress notes. Fee: $322.77 + $10.15/bed per biennium.

checklist.phase: PHASE 10 — OPTIONAL SPECIALTY LICENSES (LNS, ECC, LMH)
checklist.task: Extended Congregate Care (ECC) license
checklist.instructions: Facilities licensed under 2 years get a provisional ECC license of no more than 6 months, then an unannounced inspection. The administrator needs 2 years of qualifying experience (a bachelor's degree can substitute for 1 year). Staff or contract a nurse. Monthly nursing assessments, quarterly service plan review, adequate awake staff at all hours. Training: 4 hrs administrator and ECC supervisor, 2 hrs direct care staff. Fee: $546.07 + $10.15/bed.

checklist.phase: PHASE 10 — OPTIONAL SPECIALTY LICENSES (LNS, ECC, LMH)
checklist.task: Limited Mental Health (LMH) license — required before admitting any mental health resident
checklist.instructions: Requires a standard license and no uncorrected violations. Administrator and direct-contact staff need 6 hours of DCF-approved mental health training within 6 months, then 3 hours CE every two years. Keep each resident's community living support plan and cooperative agreement. No extra AHCA fee.

corrections_vs_previous: The old report said ALF rules were in FAC 58A-5. They were renumbered to 59A-36 on 7/1/2019 (e.g., staffing 59A-36.010, formerly 58A-5.019).

The old report listed Medicaid ALF 'tiers' of $77.81/$99.30/$128.87 per day, plus a 10% dementia add-on, an $8/day behavioral add-on and a 5% rural add-on. No such state table exists. SMMC LTC plans negotiate rates with each facility (s. 409.982, F.S.). The public Medicaid ACS rate is $15.58/day (2026).

The old report gave the initial license fee as $1,000, $1,400 and $1,565–$2,000 in different places. AHCA charges $387.73 + $64.96 per private-pay bed (OSS exempt) plus a $2/bed assessment, which is $789.49 for 6 beds.

The old report said staffing was '42 direct care staff hours per 20 residents weekly.' The actual rule is a weekly-hours table (168 hrs for 0–5 residents, 212 for 6–15, 253 for 16–25 …). The 42-hour increment applies only per 20 residents above 95.
The old report said administrator CE was 'minimum 10 hours annually' (and elsewhere 12 annually). The statute and rule require 12 hours every 2 years (s. 429.52(5), F.S.).

The old report described a '1,000-hour Administrator in Training' and 40-hour mandatory staff initial training. Neither exists in rule. The rule requires a 2-hour preservice orientation plus specific in-service hours (Rule 59A-36.011).

The old report cited 'Florida Medicaid wage requirements' of $15/hr, 'Centennial Care' as a Florida plan, and plan market shares. Centennial Care is New Mexico's program. Plan shares are unsourced. Florida's minimum wage is $15.00 from 9/30/2026 by constitutional amendment.

The old report said 'only 30% of ALFs participate in Medicaid,' cited 3,609 providers and 340,000 residents, and gave a 66% turnover figure. None of these are sourced. NCAL reports 2,968 communities and 117,384 beds.
The old report gave a 40 sq ft per resident minimum citing 59A-36.025. That rule is the emergency power rule, which uses 20 net sq ft per resident for the cooled area.

The old checklist cited 'Form 3110-1023' as the ALF application. The current ALF application is AHCA Form 3110-1008 (Aug 2023). The checklist also said certificates 'must list AHCA as certificate holder,' required a 100% surety bond for any resident funds handled, and cited 59A-36.017/.016 for policies. Those rules were repealed in 2021. Bond amounts are twice monthly income under s. 429.27(2).

The old P&L defaulted to California rates and wages. Its 'Florida' row ($4,500/mo, $16.18/hr from BLS May 2024) is outdated. CareScout 2025 Florida median is $5,500/mo, and the BLS May 2025 FL median aide wage is $16.25.
